title: The US and Russia: groundhog diplomacy
gist: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's 5-6 September 2026 trip to Moscow and Kyiv restarted US mediation of Russia's war in Ukraine, but Moscow simply repeated its maximalist terms while hardening on the ground - more missile production, Black Sea attacks on grain shipping, and sub-threshold sabotage inside NATO. The author argues the war therefore cannot end soon, sanctions relief is off the table while other US officials (Ratcliffe, Bessent) deliver warnings, and Trump's closest envoys lack any working theory of how the war ends.

themes.theme: Kyiv visit as a precedent shift

insights.claim: Witkoff and Kushner's 6 September 2026 stop in Kyiv was their first-ever trip to the Ukrainian capital as US envoys and establishes an expectation that any future Moscow visit must be mirrored by one to Kyiv.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: A procedural precedent that raises Ukraine's floor in any negotiation - watch whether subsequent US envoy travel keeps the Moscow-Kyiv pairing, as breaking it would signal a US tilt toward a bilateral deal over Ukraine's head.
insights.quote: It also sets a precedent and establishes an expectation that any future visit to Moscow should be mirrored by one to Kyiv.
insights.locator: The Kyiv leg of the trip was the only significant development

insights.claim: The Kremlin's core diplomatic objective is to frame Russia's war in Ukraine as a matter to be settled by Russia and the United States alone, so direct US engagement with Kyiv is a setback to Moscow rather than a neutral procedural step.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Any format change that reinstates bilateral US-Russia talks without Ukraine is a leading indicator that Washington is moving toward terms Kyiv will reject - and toward a prolonged rather than settled conflict.
insights.quote: Conversely, it was unwelcome to the Kremlin, which has sought to frame the war as an issue to be decided by Russia and the United States alone.
insights.locator: Conversely, it was unwelcome to the Kremlin

insights.claim: Russia may have struck Kyiv's two main airports specifically to block a direct Moscow-to-Kyiv flight by the US envoys, indicating Moscow is willing to use kinetic force to shape the diplomatic format itself.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Signals that Russian strike targeting is tied to diplomatic calendars - expect escalation around, not ahead of, negotiation milestones.
insights.quote: Russia may have tried to prevent it by attacking Kyiv’s two main airports to prevent a direct flight from Moscow.
insights.locator: Russia may have tried to prevent it

insights.claim: Russia runs a fixed and repeatable negotiating formula in talks with US envoys - effusive warmth, maximalist demands and complete inflexibility - so the tone of a Moscow meeting carries no information about its substance.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Discount headlines about 'constructive' or 'warm' US-Russia meetings; only a documented reduction in Russian territorial and political demands should move risk pricing on Ukraine exposure.
insights.quote: Russia repeated the same formula as in previous rounds of fruitless talks: effusive warmth, maximalist demands and complete inflexibility.
insights.locator: By contrast, the Moscow leg of the visit was Groundhog Day

insights.claim: Russia's standing terms are Ukrainian withdrawal from the Donbas, caps on the size of Ukraine's armed forces, foreign-policy non-alignment, and 'demilitarisation and denazification' - which the author reads as installation of a Kremlin-friendly regime rather than a security arrangement.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: These are regime-change terms, not border terms - which means a negotiated ceasefire is far less probable than headline diplomacy implies.
insights.quote: ‘demilitarisation and denazification’ – that is, the imposition of a Kremlin-friendly regime
insights.locator: It continued to demand Ukraine’s withdrawal from the Donbas

insights.claim: Because Russia's demands remain unacceptable to the large majority of Ukrainians, the war will continue until those demands are scaled back - making Russian concession, not Ukrainian exhaustion or US mediation, the binding constraint on any end to the fighting.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Price a multi-quarter continuation of the war as the base case; the single variable worth monitoring is any softening of Moscow's stated terms, not the frequency of talks.
insights.quote: Until they are scaled back, the continuation of the war is inevitable.
insights.locator: These demands remain unacceptable to the large majority of Ukrainians

insights.claim: US mediation on Ukraine went dormant after February 2026 because it was displaced by the war in the Middle East, making the September 2026 trip the first envoy visit to Moscow since January 2026.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: US diplomatic bandwidth is the scarce resource - a re-escalation in the Middle East would again stall Ukraine diplomacy and extend the war's duration risk premium.
insights.quote: Intense efforts in the summer and autumn of 2025 were displaced after February 2026 by the war in the Middle East.
insights.locator: The visit of Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow

insights.claim: Russian sources now insist that even if the war ends, Russian forces would continue to occupy Ukrainian territory beyond the regions Moscow explicitly claims - a hardening of terms relative to earlier rounds.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Moscow's reservation price is rising, not falling, as talks resume - a structural argument against positioning for a near-term settlement or reconstruction trade.
insights.quote: Russian sources now insist that, in the event of an end to the war, Russian forces would continue to occupy Ukrainian territory beyond the regions it explicitly seeks to control.
insights.locator: Russia’s hardening position

insights.claim: Russia is deliberately diverting resources into missile production to exploit Ukraine's shortage of air-defence interceptors, with severe strikes on Kyiv and a threat of more over the winter.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Interceptor supply is the pressure point - watch Western air-defence munition production and transfer announcements, and expect winter strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure to be the escalation vector.
insights.quote: Russia is diverting resources to missile production to exploit Ukraine’s lack of interceptors and subject Kyiv to severe attacks, with the threat of more over the winter.
insights.locator: Secondly, Russia is diverting resources to missile production

insights.claim: Since May 2026 Russia has stepped up attacks on third-party-flagged vessels carrying Ukrainian grain through the Black Sea to world markets.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Direct read-through to marine war-risk insurance premia and to agricultural commodity supply from the Black Sea corridor; attacks on neutral-flagged hulls also widen the set of states with standing to respond.
insights.quote: since May 2026 Russia has also stepped up its attacks on third-party-flagged vessels in the Black Sea carrying Ukrainian grain to world markets
insights.locator: Thirdly, since May 2026

insights.claim: An explosive-packed drone was discovered on 4 August 2026 near Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport, a major NATO logistics hub, which the author treats as a new level in Russia's sub-threshold aggression campaign against Europe.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Russian risk is no longer contained to Ukraine's borders - European logistics, infrastructure and defence-security spending are the second-order exposures, and repeated incidents raise the odds of an Article 4/5 debate.
insights.quote: marks a new level of threat in Russia’s campaign of sub-threshold aggression against Europe
insights.locator: The discovery on 4 August of an explosive-packed drone

themes.theme: Russia's own attrition and the authoritarian trap

insights.claim: Putin's strategy rests on the frequently stated belief that Russia's underlying economic and demographic advantage will let it outlast both Ukraine's defence and European support for Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: The war is being fought as an endurance bet on European political staying power - so European defence funding commitments, not battlefield lines, are the variable that would force Moscow to reprice.
insights.quote: Putin’s frequently expressed confidence that Russia’s underlying economic and demographic advantage will enable it to outlast Ukraine’s defence and European support for it
insights.locator: These actions in turn reflect Putin’s frequently expressed confidence

insights.claim: Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian oil facilities have compelled the introduction of widespread fuel rationing inside Russia.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Refinery strikes are hitting Russian domestic distribution hard enough to force rationing - a live channel into Russian product exports, crack spreads and domestic political tolerance for the war.
insights.quote: conducting long-range attacks on oil facilities that have compelled the introduction of widespread fuel rationing
insights.locator: But Russia, too, faces growing difficulties

insights.claim: Ukraine is simultaneously inflicting enormous Russian manpower losses and using middle-range strikes to suppress Russian resupply to Crimea, meaning Russia's position is deteriorating even as its negotiating stance hardens.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: The divergence between Russia's worsening material position and its stiffening terms is the key anomaly - it implies Moscow's demands are driven by information failure or politics, not by battlefield leverage.
insights.locator: Ukraine is inflicting enormous manpower losses

insights.claim: Russia may be caught in an authoritarian trap in which harsh repression rewards subordinates for exaggerating successes and concealing bad news from the leader, producing flawed strategic decision-making at the top.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: A reusable model for forecasting autocracies: if the decision-maker is misinformed, rational-actor models of Russian concession will keep failing, and policy errors - including escalation against NATO - become more likely, not less.
insights.quote: Russia may be falling into an authoritarian trap, whereby a harshly repressive system creates strong incentives to exaggerate successes and conceal unwelcome truths from the leader.
insights.locator: It is not clear how informed Putin is

insights.claim: Putin has repeatedly announced publicly that Russian forces have captured towns and cities that Ukraine still controls, which the author treats as concrete evidence that the Russian leader is being misinformed.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Treat Russian official battlefield claims as an unreliable data source for both analysts and, apparently, for the Kremlin itself.
insights.quote: He has repeatedly announced that Russian forces have taken towns and cities still controlled by Ukraine.
insights.locator: He has repeatedly announced that Russian forces

insights.claim: CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow roughly two weeks before the envoys' trip, reportedly to warn Russia against escalating its sabotage campaign in Europe and to share a bleak US assessment of Russia's position in the war.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: The intelligence channel is delivering deterrence messaging in parallel with the envoy channel's dealmaking - a divided US signal that Moscow can arbitrage.
insights.locator: Two weeks ago CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow

insights.claim: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov that sanctions would not be eased until the war had ended, tying sanctions relief to termination of the war rather than to progress in talks.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Removes the near-term sanctions-relief optionality from Russia-exposed assets: diplomacy alone does not unlock relief, only an actual end to the war does.
insights.quote: Last week US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov that sanctions would not be eased until the war had ended.
insights.locator: Last week US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent

insights.claim: Witkoff and Kushner, the officials closest to President Trump, do not understand the essential character of the war and therefore lack a coherent theory of how it could end - in particular they have not grasped that any settlement must give Russia far less than the effective political control of Ukraine it seeks.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: The people with the most access to the US president are, on this reading, the least equipped to close a deal - a reason to fade optimism generated by envoy-level diplomacy.
insights.quote: they have not grasped that this will require Russia to accept a settlement that gives it far less than the effective political control of Ukraine it seeks
insights.locator: But Witkoff and Kushner – the officials closest to President Donald Trump

insights.claim: Ending the war requires an idiom of warning and constraint toward Moscow rather than the win-win dealmaking frame the US envoys are applying, so their future visits are likely to be just as fruitless as previous rounds.
insights.speaker: Nigel Gould-Davies
insights.so_what: Expect repeated headline diplomacy with no settlement; only a visible shift in US tactics toward coercive pressure - more sanctions, more weapons, explicit threats - would change the probability distribution on a ceasefire.
insights.quote: Nor do they see that warning and constraint, not win–win, is the necessary idiom.
insights.locator: Nor do they see that warning and constraint
